result: TLR13 detects bacterial 23S ribosomal RNA with exquisite sequence specificity, recognizing a 13-nucleotide sequence (ISR23) near the active site of the 23S rRNA ribozyme. Single point mutations within this sequence destroy TLR13 activation, and TLR13 knockout abolishes cytokine induction by this RNA sequence.

result: The high sequence specificity of TLR13 may allow effective bacterial detection while minimizing autoimmunity, though bacteria could potentially escape detection through mutations. Humans may have abandoned TLR13 to avoid autoimmune risks and allow commensal bacterial colonization.
